E2.evidence: Step 1: tf's view_frames reaches tf2 through tf::Transformer::allFramesAsDot(), which at geometry 1.10.5 is 'return tf2_buffer_._allFramesAsDot();', so the units are the tf package (caller) and the tf2 library (BufferCore). Step 2: the crash is inside tf2's own logic and would occur with any correct caller. At the parent revision d5eba17, BufferCore::_allFramesAsDot dereferences the cache pointer unconditionally: 'if(  getFrame(counter)->getData(ros::Time(), temp))', while BufferCore::lookupOrInsertFrameNumber inserts a null placeholder for every frame name it has seen ('frames_.push_back(TimeCacheInterfacePtr());//Just a place holder for iteration') and allocateFrame only replaces it when a transform with that child frame is set; a frame referenced only as a parent therefore has a null TimeCacheInterfacePtr and the dot generation dereferences it. The merged change adds the missing null checks: '+    TimeCacheInterfacePtr counter_frame = getFrame(counter);' / '+    if (!counter_frame) {' / '+      continue;' / '+    }' (https://github.com/ros/geometry2/commit/6c13c78a9fd4a9220867f8433243deb00a8d7eb6). No value, frame, name, definition, or timing crossing the tf/tf2 boundary is wrong; the caller passes nothing that could avoid it, and the fix changes no declared or referenced interface. The ROBUST record locates it likewise: 'calling BufferCore::lookupOrInsertFrameNumber with some messy string will put a NULL object in the back that should cause the trouble'.
